newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-MONGIA CENTURY PUTS INDIA ON TOP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MONGIA CENTURY PUTS INDIA ON TOP.

text.p: Nayan Mongia's maiden test
century put India in command on the second day against Australia
on Friday.
The opener and wicketkeper hit 137 not out and led India to
a second day total of 319 for six, 137 ahead on first innings,
in the one-off test.
Mongia's previous highest score in 13 tests was 80 against
West Indies at Bombay in 1994.
He received admirable support from Saurav Ganguly, who made
66. The pair added 131 for the second wicket on the slow pitch.
Rahul Dravid arrived after captain Sachin Tendulkar and
Mohammed Azharuddin fell cheaply and put on 61 with Mongia for
the fifth wicket.
Dravid was out for 40 to the second delivery with the second
new ball from Steve Waugh. Wicketkeeper Ian Healy dived full
length for a brilliant catch.
Mongia's unbeaten 137 came in 442 minutes off 323 balls with
17 fours. He reached his 100 in 327 minutes from 229 deliveries
with 13 fours.
He said doubling as an opener and a wicketkeeper was tough.
"It is mentally and physically tiring to keep wicket as well as
open the innings in international cricket."
Mongia was dropped at 96 by Mark Waugh at first slip off leg
spinner Peter McIntyre.
